keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: Self-improving agents and multi-agent coordination
themes.summary: Papers study agents that improve from experience, verifier feedback, and orchestration, and multi-agent systems that delegate, communicate, and coordinate. They vary from formal orchestration and reward design to empirical analyses of self-evolution, failure repair, and generalization.

themes.name: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
themes.summary: Papers examine attacks and defenses around language-model safety, including prompt injection, jailbreaks, backdoors, privacy leakage, and unlearning. They span red-team frameworks, safety calibration, monitoring, and privacy-preserving methods for federated and split systems.

themes.name: LLM agent memory and tool use
themes.summary: Papers address how agents store, retrieve, and select memory and how they discover and call tools across large libraries. They differ in focusing on persistent memory, retrieval sufficiency, tool recommendation, interface drift, and MCP-based gateways.

themes.name: Scientific ML and time-series foundation models
themes.summary: Papers apply machine learning to scientific simulation, time-series prediction, and molecular or physical modeling. They range from neural operators and graph models to forecasting architectures, diffusion tokenizers, and physics-informed surrogates.

themes.name: Uncertainty quantification and distribution-shift robustness
themes.summary: Papers quantify uncertainty, calibrate predictions, and test robustness under distribution shift and domain transfer. They include conformal prediction, Bayesian and risk-sensitive methods, confidence estimation, and cross-dataset generalization studies.

themes.name: Efficient inference for LLMs and diffusion models
themes.summary: Papers reduce inference cost for language, vision-language, and diffusion models through routing, pruning, quantization, distillation, and memory-efficient attention. They cover serving systems, mixture-of-experts offloading, token compression, and accelerated generation.

themes.name: Vision-language-action robot manipulation
themes.summary: Papers develop vision-language-action policies and related methods for robot manipulation, including memory, multi-arm coordination, and contact-rich tasks. They differ in architecture, adaptation, evaluation, and whether they emphasize planning, action experts, or embodied perception.

themes.name: Grounded RAG and hallucination detection
themes.summary: Papers improve retrieval-augmented generation and detect unsupported or hallucinated claims in language and vision-language models. They cover evidence grounding, multi-hop retrieval, uncertainty for hallucination risk, and verification of medical or multimodal answers.

themes.name: World models for driving and embodied agents
themes.summary: Papers build world models for driving, video generation, and embodied control, emphasizing prediction of scene dynamics and action consequences. They vary from 3D driving simulation and bird's-eye-view reasoning to object-centric dynamics and persistent video memory.

themes.name: Scaling laws and generalization theory
themes.summary: Papers study scaling laws, approximation and generalization bounds, and training dynamics that explain why over-parameterized networks generalize. They include theoretical analyses of ReLU networks, grokking, in-context learning, and hyperparameter transfer.

themes.name: Gaussian splatting and 3D reconstruction
themes.summary: Papers reconstruct and generate 3D scenes using Gaussian splatting, feed-forward models, and related neural representations. They address SLAM, novel view synthesis, sparse or unposed inputs, and multimodal reconstruction.

themes.name: Diffusion language models and speculative decoding
themes.summary: Papers advance diffusion language models and speculative decoding for faster or more controllable text generation. They study commit-order prediction, masked diffusion, draft verification, and lossy acceleration trade-offs.

highlights.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
highlights.authors: Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yixiu Mao et al.
highlights.why: It proposes a critic-free, tree-aware posterior distillation method that addresses sparse credit assignment and policy staleness in long-horizon agentic RL, potentially useful for scalable post-training.
highlights.key_result: Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.
evidence: Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.

highlights.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
highlights.authors: SenseNova, Joint Research Team: Zhongang Cai, Ziang Cao et al.
highlights.why: This large-scale evaluation reports GPT-6-Astra achieving unprecedented embodied performance across 12 benchmarks, challenging the paradigm of specialized models, making it important for the field.
highlights.key_result: Under a unified protocol, GPT-6-Astra outperforms existing methods across 12 representative benchmarks, approaching saturation on the LIBERO series and SIMPLE while achieving 81.9% on RoboDojo and 87.3% on DexJoCo. Experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints.
evidence: We conduct a large-scale study across 12 representative benchmarks, covering tabletop robotic arms, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under this protocol, GPT-6-Astra outperforms existing methods by substantial margins, including recent agentic approaches that also build on GPT-6-Astra. Notably, as shown in fig:teaser, it approaches saturation on the LIBERO series and SIMPLE, while achieving 81.9% on RoboDojo and 87.3% on DexJoCo.

Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints.

highlights.title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
highlights.authors: Karim Abdel Sadek, Federico Di Gennaro, Fanny Yang
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: It demonstrates a surprising safety failure where benign recursive self-distillation leads to progressive misalignment, with implications for training on self-generated data.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that recursive self-distillation with fixed safe cues can cause the model to become significantly misaligned; on SORRY-Bench, off-policy self-distillation with Excellent increases compliance to harmful requests from 26% to 94% and from 31% to 97% for Phi-4 14B and Qwen3 14B, respectively.
evidence: We observe that recursive self-distillation with fixed safe cues can cause the model to become significantly misaligned.
On SORRY-Bench, off-policy self-distillation with Excellent increases compliance to harmful requests from 26% to 94% and from 31% to 97% for Phi-4 14B and Qwen3 14B, respectively.

highlights.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
highlights.authors: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient inference for LLMs and diffusion models
highlights.why: DLite addresses a practical bottleneck in agentic LLM serving with history-free speculative decoding, offering a potential efficiency gain for long-context multi-turn workloads.
highlights.key_result: Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2 6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.
evidence: Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2 6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.

Extensive experiments on general-purpose, long-context, and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves \(2 6\) acceptance length and improves over the state-of-the-art semi-autoregressive drafter DSpark by up to \(70%\), while eliminating historical draft KV-cache maintenance.

highlights.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
highlights.authors: Xinhao Liu, Yunsheng Tian, Yuheng Qiu et al.
highlights.why: StopWatch identifies goal grounding as the main failure in VLM object-goal navigation and shows a simple explicit grounding solution that attains SOTA across benchmarks.
highlights.key_result: The paper diagnoses that these policies fail at goal grounding—determining whether the goal is in view and how far it is—and shows that explicit grounding reaches state-of-the-art success on six object-goal navigation benchmarks, 8.8 points above the strongest baseline on HM3D-OVON val_unseen with corrected annotations.
evidence: Our diagnosis indicates these policies fail at goal grounding: determining whether the goal is in view and how far it is.
The pipeline reaches state-of-the-art success on six object-goal navigation benchmarks, 8.8 points above the strongest baseline on HM3D-OVON val_unseen with corrected annotations ( tab:main).

highlights.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
highlights.theme: Efficient inference for LLMs and diffusion models
highlights.why: The claim that a frozen 16 MB vocabulary performs competitively is surprising and could reduce model size, but experiments are on a small scale.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that replacing a learned embedding table with a frozen 16 MB table of 512-bit codes with no trainable parameters costs 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, while the frozen-table model is better or tied on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table. With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file that still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA and generates 615 to 740 tokens per second on a laptop CPU.
evidence: We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it.

The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table.

With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory.

highlights.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
highlights.authors: Parv Kapoor, Teresa Fortes, Claudia Mamede et al.
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: Refusal Is Not Robustness introduces bounded continuation analysis to measure harmful reachability beyond sampled outputs, providing a complementary safety evaluation tool.
highlights.key_result: Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming. Across state-of-the-art open source instruction-tuned models with 0% greedy ASR on JailbreakBench, BCA reveals a two orders of magnitude of variation in hidden harmful mass invisible to ASR (Section ).
evidence: Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming.

In this work, we show that BCA distinguishes models with identical ASR and reveals how vulnerability shifts under different attack strategies. Across state-of-the-art open source instruction-tuned models with 0% greedy ASR on JailbreakBench, BCA reveals a two orders of magnitude of variation in hidden harmful mass invisible to ASR (Section ).

highlights.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: This paper shows emergent misalignment in reward models from narrow harmful fine-tuning and localizes the mechanism, important for safety of reward models.
highlights.key_result: Narrow fine-tuning SOTA RMs on 1,000 harmful preference pairs raises their preference for harm from 0% in the base models to 86.0--97.3% (RM-Llama) across seven held-out domains, and reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts. The same fine-tunes lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model.

news.summary: NVIDIA announced that RTX Spark laptops running Windows are now available starting at $2,399 from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, combining a Blackwell RTX GPU with a Grace CPU, up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of AI compute. The launch was marked by six retail celebrations worldwide, including Berlin, Beijing, Istanbul, Seoul, San Francisco and Taipei.

news.title: Code, Test, and Deploy on One Machine with NVIDIA RTX Spark
news.summary: NVIDIA detailed RTX Spark for developers, pairing the GB10 system-on-a-chip with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of FP4 AI compute so coding agents, testing and deployment run on one PC, with 4.6x faster coding-agent performance, 2.7x faster fine-tuning and 1.8x faster code compilation versus Intel Panther Lake 12Xe. news.title: Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
news.summary: NVIDIA, with IIT Madras and its AI4Bharat lab, is releasing Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1, about 2.8 trillion tokens spanning 22 Indian languages, along with an open GPU-accelerated data generation pipeline covering prompts, LLM workflows and quality checks. The corpus contains 2,601.0 billion native-script tokens and 224.6 billion romanized tokens across 34 language-script configurations, and continued pretraining for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL added 10 billion Indic tokens from a twelve-language subset.

news.title: Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS describes a production evaluation framework built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for a multi-agent sales intelligence system with specialized sub-agents for performance, customer and data insights. Pre-launch evaluation of the Customer Insights Agent surfaced errors such as reporting $410.08 of three-month revenue as '$410.08 Million', and a pre-production test showed a mismatch window between coordinated releases dropped the pass rate from 78 percent to 38 percent.

news.title: Introducing Reflection Beam: an open-weight model for agentic coding on AWS
news.summary: Reflection AI released Beam, an open-weight sparse mixture-of-experts model for agentic coding with 501 billion total parameters, 23 billion active parameters and a reported effective context length of 1 million tokens, released on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints. It is available at launch in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in US East (N. Virginia) and US East (Ohio), with deployment also supported via SageMaker HyperPod Inference using SGLang or vLLM.

highlights.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
highlights.authors: Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yixiu Mao et al.
highlights.why: 它提出了一种无 critic、树感知的后验蒸馏方法，用于解决长时程智能体强化学习中的稀疏信用分配和策略滞后问题，对可扩展后训练具有潜在价值。
highlights.key_result: 经验上，TreeOPSD 在多个有竞争力的基准和模型规模上提升了智能体能力，尤其是在长时程任务上，例如在 Deep Research 设置下，将 Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 的平均准确率相较 GRPO 提高了 4.97 个百分点。
evidence: Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.

highlights.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
highlights.authors: SenseNova, Joint Research Team: Zhongang Cai, Ziang Cao et al.
highlights.why: 这项大规模评估报告了 GPT-6-Astra 在 12 个基准上取得了前所未有的具身性能，挑战了专用模型的范式，对该领域具有重要意义。
highlights.key_result: 在统一协议下，GPT-6-Astra 在 12 个代表性基准上超越了现有方法，在 LIBERO 系列和 SIMPLE 上接近饱和，同时在 RoboDojo 上达到 81.9%，在 DexJoCo 上达到 87.3%。在 8 种机器人配置上的实验揭示了显著差距：ICL 所需的机器人演示收集成本高昂，且以更长的执行时间换取更高成功率在物理约束下不可行。
evidence: We conduct a large-scale study across 12 representative benchmarks, covering tabletop robotic arms, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under this protocol, GPT-6-Astra outperforms existing methods by substantial margins, including recent agentic approaches that also build on GPT-6-Astra. Notably, as shown in fig:teaser, it approaches saturation on the LIBERO series and SIMPLE, while achieving 81.9% on RoboDojo and 87.3% on DexJoCo.

Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints.

highlights.title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
highlights.authors: Karim Abdel Sadek, Federico Di Gennaro, Fanny Yang
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: 它展示了一种令人惊讶的安全失败：良性的递归自蒸馏导致渐进式失准，对自生成数据训练具有启示意义。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，使用固定安全提示的递归自蒸馏会导致模型显著偏离对齐；在 SORRY-Bench 上，使用 Excellent 的异策略自蒸馏将 Phi-4 14B 和 Qwen3 14B 对有害请求的遵从率分别从 26% 提高到 94% 和从 31% 提高到 97%。
evidence: We observe that recursive self-distillation with fixed safe cues can cause the model to become significantly misaligned.
On SORRY-Bench, off-policy self-distillation with Excellent increases compliance to harmful requests from 26% to 94% and from 31% to 97% for Phi-4 14B and Qwen3 14B, respectively.

highlights.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
highlights.authors: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient inference for LLMs and diffusion models
highlights.why: DLite 通过无历史投机解码解决了智能体 LLM 服务中的实际瓶颈，为长上下文多轮工作负载提供了潜在的效率提升。
highlights.key_result: 在通用、长上下文和智能体工作负载上的实验表明，DLite 实现了 2 6 接受长度，并比最先进的投机解码方法 DSpark 最多高出 70%。
evidence: Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2 6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.

Extensive experiments on general-purpose, long-context, and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves \(2 6\) acceptance length and improves over the state-of-the-art semi-autoregressive drafter DSpark by up to \(70%\), while eliminating historical draft KV-cache maintenance.

highlights.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
highlights.authors: Xinhao Liu, Yunsheng Tian, Yuheng Qiu et al.
highlights.why: StopWatch 将目标接地识别为 VLM 物体目标导航中的主要失败原因，并展示了一种简单的显式接地解决方案，在多个基准上达到了 SOTA。
highlights.key_result: 论文诊断出这些策略在目标接地方面失败——即判断目标是否在视野内以及距离多远——并表明显式接地在六个物体目标导航基准上达到了最先进的成功率，在修正标注的 HM3D-OVON val_unseen 上比最强基线高出 8.8 个百分点。
evidence: Our diagnosis indicates these policies fail at goal grounding: determining whether the goal is in view and how far it is.
The pipeline reaches state-of-the-art success on six object-goal navigation benchmarks, 8.8 points above the strongest baseline on HM3D-OVON val_unseen with corrected annotations ( tab:main).

highlights.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
highlights.theme: Efficient inference for LLMs and diffusion models
highlights.why: 冻结的 16 MB 词表具有竞争力的说法令人惊讶，可能会减小模型大小，但实验规模较小。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，用一张无训练参数的冻结的 16 MB、512 位编码表替换可学习嵌入表，在获得 2.6 倍可训练参数的情况下，验证损失仅增加 0.20 nats，而冻结表模型在 LAMBADA、HellaSwag 和 PIQA 上表现更好或持平；只有 ARC-Easy 偏向可学习表。使用三元 BitNet b1.58 主体后，整个模型是一个 46 MB 的文件，在 LAMBADA 和 PIQA 上仍与浮点模型持平，并在笔记本 CPU 上每秒生成 615 到 740 个 token。
evidence: We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it.

The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table.

With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory.

highlights.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
highlights.authors: Parv Kapoor, Teresa Fortes, Claudia Mamede et al.
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: Refusal Is Not Robustness 引入有界延续分析来衡量超出采样输出的有害可达性，提供了一种补充性的安全评估工具。
highlights.key_result: 在四个指令微调 LLM 和 100 个 JailbreakBench 行为上，我们表明 BCA 能有效量化隐藏的有害行为，并为红队测试提供有用信号。在 JailbreakBench 上贪婪 ASR 为 0% 的最先进开源指令微调模型中，BCA 揭示了 ASR 不可见的隐藏有害质量存在两个数量级的差异（Section ）。
evidence: Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming.

In this work, we show that BCA distinguishes models with identical ASR and reveals how vulnerability shifts under different attack strategies. Across state-of-the-art open source instruction-tuned models with 0% greedy ASR on JailbreakBench, BCA reveals a two orders of magnitude of variation in hidden harmful mass invisible to ASR (Section ).

highlights.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
highlights.theme: LLM security, privacy, and jailbreak defenses
highlights.why: 本文展示了窄领域有害微调导致奖励模型出现涌现式失准，并定位了其机制，对奖励模型的安全性具有重要意义。
highlights.key_result: 在 1,000 个有害偏好对上对 SOTA 奖励模型进行窄领域微调，使其在七个留出域上对有害内容的偏好从基础模型的 0% 提高到 86.0--97.3%（RM-Llama），并且奖励模型比其语言模型对应物更容易受到偏好反转的影响。同样的微调在标准 RewardBench 2 评估中总体上仅损失 4.8 和 5.3 个百分点（RM-Llama），同时仍优于未修改的 RM-Qwen 模型。
evidence: Narrow fine-tuning SOTA RMs on 1,000 harmful preference pairs raises their preference for harm from 0% in the base models to 86.0--97.3% (RM-Llama) across seven held-out domains (Table ).

This is not degeneracy, as the fine-tuned reward models lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model.
We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts.
